subject: POC trial environment setup (hosted vs dedicated vs VPC) - post-call recap
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acme.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: POC trial environment setup (hosted vs dedicated vs VPC) - post-call recap

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed plan so we have alignment before the kickoff: 

Call highlights / goals
- Acme AI wants to validate Redwood for production inference for chat + embeddings workloads.
- Primary requirements: data isolation (no cross-tenant leakage), configurable KMS, SOC2 evidence for procurement, and <250ms p95 for short prompts (<=512 tokens).
- Target evaluation window: 2-4 weeks, start of trial targeted for the first week of March.

Success criteria (proposed)
1) Functional: integration with your backend (API calls + SDK), embedding quality parity with your baseline on our eval set (benchmark pass threshold TBD).
2) Performance: p95 latency <250ms for 256-token prompts at expected QPS (see below).
3) Security/compliance: VPC or dedicated environment with KMS integration + audit logs; SOC2 artifact exchange completed.
4) Operability: ability to sustain 50 QPS with acceptable token costs; auto-scaling behavior observed.

Evaluation plan / timeline
- By Feb 22: finalize environment choice (hosted sandbox vs dedicated sandbox vs VPC).
- Feb 23-26: infra prep and account provisioning (test keys, allowlist, KMS setup).
- Mar 1: POC kickoff and baseline run (smoke tests + eval prompts).
- Mar 1-Mar 14: validation window (metrics, logs, and weekly syncs).

Ownership
- Redwood: Marissa (program lead), Neha (SE / infra lead) - provisioning, SOC2 artifacts, SLO monitoring dashboards.
- Acme AI: Sarah (product lead), infra@acme.ai (network & security).

Environment options (short primer)
- Hosted sandbox: fastest to start; we host, limited network restrictions, good for functional + perf sampling but not ideal if you need strict VPC-only access.
- Dedicated sandbox: reserved GPU pool for Acme only (no tenant neighbors), single-tenant runtime, supports KMS; lower setup overhead than full VPC.
- VPC trial (Private): customer-managed networking (VPC peering / PrivateLink), full network isolation, recommended for regulated workloads. Longer setup and on-boarding.

Next steps (please confirm):
1) Confirm preferred environment option (reply in-thread).
2) Share a contact for infra/team who can accept a short network questionnaire (CIDRs, egress policy, expected QPS).
3) If VPC: share preferred timeline for peering windows.
4) I’ve attached our Redwood POC setup guide and a SOW template for quick review.

Thanks - happy to jump on a short follow-up with your infra team if helpful.

Best,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa - this is really helpful and aligns with what we discussed. A few notes from our side: 

- We are leaning strongly toward a VPC trial due to our compliance posture (must have customer-managed KMS and no public egress to hosted endpoints).
- Expected baseline traffic for the POC: ~20-50 QPS for embeddings during batch runs and 10-20 QPS for chat traffic during peak tests.
- Timeline: we are aiming to kick things off around Mar 1 but have a short procurement review that needs the SOW and SOC2 artifacts. If we can get the SOW and SOC2 evidence in the next 48 hours that would accelerate approval.

I’ve attached our network diagram (acme_network_diagram.pdf) and looped infra@acme.ai. For peering: we prefer PrivateLink but can do VPC peering depending on constraints. Our infra team will follow up with CIDR ranges.

Also can you confirm support for AWS KMS key import/use vs partner-managed keys?

Thanks,

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acme.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: infra@acme.ai
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC trial environment setup (hosted vs dedicated vs VPC) - technical details

Hi Sarah - looping in some quick technical clarifications and what we’ll need to stand up a VPC trial: 

Thanks for the network diagram - that helps. Short answers first: 
- KMS: Redwood supports customer-managed AWS KMS keys for VPC/private deployments (you can bring your own key). We can also integrate with partner-managed keys if needed, but BYOK via your AWS account is the standard.
- Private connectivity: we support both AWS PrivateLink (preferred for lower ops) and VPC peering. For PrivateLink we expose an NLB-backed endpoint in our region and you create the interface endpoint in your VPC.

What we need from your infra team to provision a VPC trial (minimum):
1) CIDR for the interface endpoints (or confirmation to create interface endpoints).
2) List of static IPs to allowlist if your environment requires outbound egress restrictions.
3) Expected peak QPS and token mix (approx % embeddings vs chat) - helps sizing the dedicated pool if you choose that path.
4) AWS account ID + KMS key ARN (for BYOK) if you want us to configure KMS on our side.

If you prefer a dedicated sandbox (no peering required) we can reserve a single-tenant GPU pool and provide test keys and a restricted ingress allowlist; that path cuts ~3-5 business days off the setup compared to VPC. Hosted sandbox would be fastest (same-day), but again not VPC-isolated.

Sample smoke test we’ll run once provisioned:
- Auth + token exchange test
- 100 warmup requests (embedding & chat) to populate KV cache
- Latency profile (p50/p95) for 256-token prompts
- Basic throughput ramp to 50 QPS to confirm autoscaling

Happy to run a 30-minute tech kickoff with your infra folks to speed up the checklist - available Mon/Tue next week.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com
